mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its pre-pandemic median for at least 3 consecutive months, long-term discount rates for equities decline, amplifying the present value of future earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day average during comparable low-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs, accompanied by a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5%, predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as market interprets labor market strength as expansionary demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200,000 AND UNRATE falls below 3.5% within the same month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 20-day forward return correlation with the combined labor signal falls below 0.3 in absolute value.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 (pre-pandemic median) for two consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), signals resilient supply chains and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 105 for 2 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 243.8 (December 2022 value) in the same month
failure_condition: Across 50 such supply-cycle events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 240 accompanied by a rise in retail sales (HOUST) above 1,200 units in the same month predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates disinflation and resilient demand.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 240 AND HOUST > 1200 in the same month
failure_condition: In 10 such disinflationary demand episodes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly RSAFS (reserves) by over 100 million dollars coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals excess liquidity being deployed into equities, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >100M AND UNRATE < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: Across 15 such liquidity injection events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the monthly payrolls growth (PAYEMS) below 100,000 jobs for three consecutive months in the absence of a rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as market anticipates a softening labor market and reduced wage growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 100,000 for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 245 in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 such labor softening cycles, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (pre-pandemic median) for four consecutive months, without a corresponding decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), suggests supply-side weakness and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 245 in the same month
failure_condition: Across 8 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for the first time in a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a negative 20-day forward return as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5%
failure_condition: In 12 such tightening-cycle starts, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
